claims.claim: A Baseline Profile is generated and shipped.
claims.note: No Baseline Profile file, no benchmark module and no CI step.

claims.claim: CHANGELOG generated from Conventional Commits.
claims.note: No changelog file and no release tooling that would generate one.

claims.claim: compose.yml runs Navidrome plus syncd.
claims.note: The file is docker-compose.yml and it defines Navidrome only.

claims.claim: Patch-coverage gate of 80% on sync, parsers, migrations and affinity.
claims.note: No coverage flag, profile or threshold anywhere in CI or the Makefile.

claims.claim: gitleaks runs in CI and in a local pre-commit hook.
claims.note: No config, no workflow step, no pre-commit file.

claims.claim: Golden identity set from the owner runs on every resolver change.
claims.note: The test has two synthetic cases and discards the result. It cannot fail on a resolver regression.

claims.claim: golangci-lint, actionlint, zizmor and hadolint run in CI.
claims.note: The file itself says ci.yml runs build, vet and test only. .golangci.yml enables gofmt and govet.

claims.claim: Backups use restic and monitoring uses Uptime Kuma plus ntfy.
claims.note: No ops directory, backup job or monitoring config exists in the repository.

claims.claim: Property tests cover merge idempotence and order independence.
claims.note: The loop rebuilds the same two constants 1000 times and never calls Resolve or Merge.

claims.claim: Property tests use the rapid library.
claims.note: rapid is not a dependency. The only property test is a fixed loop.

claims.claim: A simulation harness runs 200 seeds per PR and 10,000 nightly.
claims.note: nightly.yml runs go test ./... only. No replica, partition or clock-jump harness exists.

claims.claim: X-Client-* headers and 426 responses are implemented.
claims.note: No server code emits or reads the headers, and no handler returns 426.

claims.claim: Gate G3 is closed and ADR-0002 is accepted without conditions.
claims.note: ADR-0002 is marked Accepted (conditional) and the phase file says owner sign-off is pending. Sign-off is not observable in the repository.

claims.claim: TestNavidromeContract validates every response against the vendored OpenAPI and records goldens.
claims.note: The test calls Ping and Albums, then stops. The OpenAPI file is never read by the test.

claims.claim: FuzzReadTagLib exercises the tag parser in the default test run.
claims.note: The fuzz target sits in a cgo-only file, so CGO_ENABLED=0 make test never compiles it.

claims.claim: The native scanner uses go-taglib.
claims.note: The scanner calls the C API directly through cgo and links libtag_c. No Go wrapper is used.

claims.claim: The native scanner is part of the default build and test run.
claims.note: Both default targets disable cgo, which excludes scanner.go and scanner_test.go.

claims.claim: The status header says the native scanner is still a gap.
claims.note: A scanner exists behind the cgo tag. The real gap is that the default build does not compile it.

claims.claim: Weekly live contract tests cover Spotify and YouTube.
claims.note: The only scheduled contract job is the Navidrome test.

claims.claim: Two weeks of shadow plans were reviewed before live was enabled.
claims.note: A two-week human run cannot be reconstructed from the tree. owner-choices.md says live Spotify tests are deferred and no run is recorded.

claims.claim: The status header says the Spotify authorization flow and encrypted storage do not exist.
claims.note: PKCE endpoints and AES-GCM token storage exist and are tested. The live owner test is still missing.

claims.claim: Backtests were run against real listening history.
claims.note: Backtest helpers exist. No real history, dataset or recorded result is in the repository.

claims.claim: ColdStartScore is wired into the HTTP scoring path.
claims.note: The function and its wrapper exist, but handleScores calls ScoreTracks only. The cold-start wrapper has no caller outside tests.

claims.claim: TestNoSpotifyFieldInContributions fails if any Spotify-sourced field reaches the score.
claims.note: The test only inspects contribution names. A Spotify value in the score or in another field would pass.

claims.claim: A manual override is stored per track, always wins and survives re-sync.
claims.note: Only the migration exists. No Go code reads or writes the table.

claims.claim: The why view is built from real contributions and every score can be explained.
claims.note: handleWhy returns an empty contributions slice and a nil override for every track.

claims.claim: The Android client lists and searches a 50k-track library.
claims.note: The library screen renders a hardcoded list of strings. There is no database, network call or real track model.

claims.claim: CI runs lint, unit, emulator smoke and Macrobenchmark.
claims.note: ci.yml builds and unit-tests the modules and checks page alignment. It runs no linter, emulator or benchmark.

claims.claim: A desktop application with a UI exists.
claims.note: The desktop module is a command-line client. It has no window, tray or Compose UI.

claims.claim: Go and the client pass the same HLC golden vector file.
claims.note: The Go test loads spec/hlc_vectors.json. The Kotlin test hardcodes two vectors and spec is not a Gradle module.

claims.claim: Cold start and jank budgets run in Macrobenchmark and CI.
claims.note: The P50, P90 and jank numbers live in a local spike document. No Macrobenchmark module or CI gate exists.

claims.claim: Media3 MediaLibraryService feeds the UI, notification and lock screen.
claims.note: No Media3 dependency and no service class in any Kotlin source set.

claims.claim: Room was chosen and the metadata mirror is implemented.
claims.note: Neither Room nor SQLDelight is declared. The db package contains plain data classes only.

claims.claim: The status header says there is no Android or desktop app source.
claims.note: Both app modules have source. They are a smoke screen and a CLI, but the header is out of date.

claims.claim: The status header says there is no worker, no provider and no second repo.
claims.note: The core worker exists and is tested but is never wired into syncd. The separate provisioner repo also exists.

claims.claim: AppImage, Flatpak, PKGBUILD, deb, rpm and Fastlane metadata are shipped.
claims.note: No packaging directory, manifest or store metadata exists.

claims.claim: Privacy policy and terms are written.
claims.note: Neither document exists. AI-POLICY.md exists and is the only published policy.

claims.claim: release-please drives the version scheme and changelog.
claims.note: No release-please config, manifest or workflow step.

claims.claim: The release produces an SBOM with syft and provenance with actions/attest.
claims.note: release.yml builds the Go packages and checks licences, then stops.

claims.claim: Android release signing, keystores and rotation are set up.
claims.note: The Android build has no signing config. Only the debug build is produced.

claims.claim: CI checks 16 KB page alignment of native libraries.
The core acquisition request API, kill switch and daily cap exist and are tested.
A Roborazzi screenshot test exists for the Android home screen.
CI builds and unit-tests the common and desktop Kotlin modules.
A scheduled Navidrome contract job exists.
claims.note: The job is real. Its coverage is narrower than the doc claims.

claims.claim: Dependabot is configured with a 14-day cooldown.
The desktop module has a CLI sync path with liked-track protection.
Spotify disconnect purges derived data.
claims.note: This is a unit test, not the five-day live test the phase file describes.

claims.claim: The Navidrome compose file drops capabilities and runs as a normal user.
A file must be stable before it is hashed.
The Go HLC implementation loads the shared vector file.
claims.note: The Kotlin side does not load the same file.

claims.claim: make check-licenses runs in CI.
Five Maestro flows exist.
claims.note: The flows target the smoke-screen app, so they do not prove the product UI works.

claims.claim: A thin OpenSubsonic client exists with JVM tests.
Core contains no extraction code and does not depend on the plugin.
The database can be rebuilt from the folder and rebuild plus upload is safe.
The review queue supports limit and offset.
Scoring keeps contributions sorted and has a cold-start path.
claims.note: The HTTP why view that should expose these contributions is a stub.

claims.claim: SECURITY.md exists with a private disclosure route and a threat model.
Go sources carry SPDX headers.
The Spotify PKCE start and complete endpoints are implemented and tested.
claims.note: The live owner test is still open.

claims.claim: Range download of a cached rendition is implemented and tested.
Resumable content-addressed upload is implemented and tested.
Connector tokens are encrypted with AES-GCM and the round trip is tested.
The folder watcher uses fsnotify and stops on context cancellation.
